title: Why Is Earth Closest to the Sun in January?
pause_note: Short format v3 (2026-11-13): 20-30 s, claim first, loop ending

beats: Earth is closest to the Sun in January.
In January we're 147 million kilometres away.
So why is January cold up north?
Distance isn't the reason. Earth is tilted.
In January the north leans away, so sunlight hits it low and weak, spread over more ground.
Closest to the Sun, and still cold.
